newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas turns buyer on Club Med.
newsitem.headline: Paribas turns buyer on Club Med.

text.p: Paribas Capital Markets analyst Nigel Reed said in a research note he had changed to a "buy" from "sell" on Club Mediterannee after key shareholders on Friday dissolved their 1990 shareholder pact.

"The result is that a bid platform/bid can be far more easily arranged," Reed wrote, saying his previous sell advice was based on no bid being possible and only looking at past and future profitability with existing management.
"We think the historic net asset value per share of 309 franc massively understates the potential value of the shares."

"The existing management (executive chairman Serge Trigano) will have to focus rapidly on improving the returns to shareholders. We wholeheartedly welcome the first indication of this, which is cutting the 1997 Summer capacity by between 2.5 and 3.0 percent mainly from the low season. Not only will this reduce budgeted variable costs, but it will help to avoid unplanned promotional spending to clear unsold holidays," Reed said in his note.
He said he believed the company should be able to make at least a 10 percent return -- at operating level -- on its gross revalued assets, which would result in a trebling of net income.
Reed said he expected a rise to at least 400 francs.
At 1359 GMT, Club Med was up 5.36 percent at 334 francs.
Club Mediterannee said on Friday in a statement that its key shareholders had ended a pact they had agreed in 1990.
The shareholders concerned are the state-bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC), Compagnie Financiere Benjamin et Edmond de Rothschild, Exor, Nippon Life Insurance Company and Rolaco.
Exor represents Italy's Agnelli family as well as sheik Abdullazziz al-Sulaiman.
The core group owned a total of 29 percent in Club Med.
Credit Lyonnais and Seibu Saison had left the pact previously.
The pact held the partners to give each other first right of refusal in case of a share sale and also limited individual stakes to 13 percent.
